item.title: This year’s Bealtaine Theatre Festival features a Ulysses adaptation and a solo show about a chicken
item.description: The 2026 edition will unfold at the Corleck, a new waterfront performance venue set to officially open in November. Bealtaine audiences will be among the first to experience the space.

item.title: REVIEW: In Montreal, Whalefall explores humanity’s fraught relationship to whales
item.description: The show feels like an act of grieving, set on a stage and shared with an audience. Rather than trying to assuage our sadness — or our guilt — Infinithéâtre’s Whalefall lets us sit with our emotions.

item.title: Spotlight: Nora McLellan
item.description: “It’s still always that same technicolour feeling for me," says McLellan. "That little girl and this much older person are pretty much the same. I really do all of my living on stage.”

item.title: REVIEW: Ronnie Burkett’s Little Willy is a love letter to theatre
item.description: Ronnie Burkett and William Shakespeare agree on at least one fundamental truth: there’s no such thing as a bad dick joke.

item.title: REVIEW: The Surrogate cross-examines privilege and parenthood at Crow’s Theatre
item.description: If the play sometimes reaches for one issue too many — religion, interracial relationships, infertility — it also underscores how interconnected these issues can be.

item.title: London’s Grand Theatre announces 2026-27 season
item.description: A Dolly Parton musical and the Canadian premiere of a drama by Matthew López are among the productions in the Grand Theatre’s 2026-27 season.

item.title: REVIEW: Mirvish’s Shucked plants row after row of corny jokes
item.description: Shucked sits somewhere between a cartoon for adults and a wholesome farm musical.

item.title: REVIEW: Jill Connell’s The Herald has a lot to say about potential
item.description: There’s so much to love about this smart, strange, and achingly lyrical exploration of labour and purpose. Dramaturgical intentionality falters, however, in the details.

item.title: REVIEW: Montreal in March? Bring on the puppets.
item.description: The 21st annual Festival International de Casteliers featured an energizing series of Quebecois and European productions that took the medium of puppetry in surprising directions.

item.title: Q&A: How Expandido Arts Collective is reimagining the Medea myth
item.description: Originally written in Portuguese as Mata Teu Pai, Passô’s play reimagines the myth of Medea through a contemporary feminist lens.
